title: Grouping & Ordering
description: Several objects behave as one: group them, stack them in order, and organise them in the Layers & Objects panel.

bubble.title: Many objects, one drawing
bubble.body: Grouping makes objects move together. Ordering decides which object paints over which. Layers organise the whole drawing.

bubble.title: Draw two overlapping shapes
bubble.body: Press I twice for one rectangle, then draw a second overlapping it. Overlap is what makes ordering visible.

bubble.title: Front and back
bubble.body: The later shape paints over the earlier one. With a shape selected, Bring to Front and Send to Back move it across the whole stack; Bring Forward and Send Backward move it one step.

bubble.title: Group the selection
bubble.body: Select both shapes (Shift-click adds to a selection) and run Group Selection, or press Cmd/Ctrl+G. The group now moves, scales and styles as one object.

bubble.title: Ungroup when you need the parts
bubble.body: Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+G ungroups. Grouping never merges the shapes — the parts come back exactly as they were.

bubble.title: Meet the Layers & Objects panel
bubble.body: The panel lists layers and every object in them. Rename objects there, hide or lock them, set opacity, and click a row to select something that is hard to click on canvas.
